title: Building a Safe Library
story: The best libraries are boring — they work every time, never surprise you, and their contracts tell you exactly what to expect. This lesson builds such a library: a small collection of math utilities, string validators, and data structures, all with ironclad contracts.
why: A well-designed library with contracts at every public function boundary is self-documenting, misuse-resistant, and a joy to use.
analogy: A safe library is like a pre-assembled toolkit from a trusted brand — every tool comes with its safety rating printed on the handle. You don't need to test each screwdriver before using it.
try_it: Export your library: create separate files for math.xi, strings.xi, and collections.xi. Add `pub` to every function and type. Then write a main.xi that imports and uses functions from all three modules. The contracts travel with the imports.
tips: Every public function gets a contract — it's the API surface your callers trust
Group related types and functions in modules named after their domain (math, strings, collections)
Internal helper functions can skip contracts IF they're only called from functions that already validate
common_mistakes: Making everything `pub` — internal helpers don't need contracts if callers already validate
Writing contracts that are too strict — 'requires: result == 42' makes the function unusable
Not testing contract violations — your library should reject bad inputs gracefully, not silently
